title: Loft by Incremental
short_description: Your own NAS in Android's Files app, through a gateway at home. No cloud.
full_description:
Loft puts the shared folders on your own NAS in Android's Files app. A small gateway runs at home, next to the NAS. No one else stores your files.

Not the cloud. The loft.

YOUR NAS, IN THE FILES APP
• Your shared folders show up in the Files app and the system file picker, so any app that opens or saves files can use them.
• Loft lists everything but only downloads what you open. When you save, the file goes back home. A big archive doesn't have to fit on a small phone.
• “Save to Loft” in the share menu sends one file or several straight to a folder on the NAS.
• Camera upload sends new photos and videos to a folder you choose, on Wi-Fi only if you like. Photos already on the phone stay where they are.
• Browse, upload, make folders, rename and delete in the app itself.

THE NAS STAYS IN CHARGE
Loft signs in to the NAS as you, with the username and password you already have. The NAS's own permissions decide what you can see and change.

YOUR FILES STAY AT HOME
There is no Loft account and no Loft server. Your files travel only between the NAS, your gateway and your own devices, and Incremental never sees your files, your file names or your password. Loft from Google Play makes no requests to us at all: no update check, no analytics, no ads. Google Play takes care of updates.

THREE STEPS
1. Install the Loft gateway on a small Linux machine at home (x86_64 or arm64, so a 64-bit Raspberry Pi will do), or run it as a container. The guide: loft.incremental.no/gateway
2. Run loft-gateway pair and scan the QR code with Loft. The code carries your gateway's keys, so the app talks to your gateway from the very first connection.
3. Sign in with your NAS username and password. Your shared folders appear in Files.

WHAT'S ENCRYPTED
• At home, the app talks to your gateway over TLS pinned to the gateway's key, so it can't be redirected to someone else's.
• Away from home, you choose. Through a tunnel, such as Cloudflare Tunnel: easy, with no open port, but the tunnel provider can read the traffic, so you sign in at home once. Or directly, with a port forwarded on your router: encrypted end to end. Or keep Loft at home only.
• Between the gateway and the NAS, Loft uses SMB 3 with encryption switched on.

WHAT YOU NEED
• A NAS or server that shares folders over SMB 3, which is what most NAS boxes, Windows servers and Samba use. Run loft-gateway doctor to check yours. What we've tested: loft.incremental.no/compatibility
• A Linux machine or container host at home for the gateway.
• Android 8 or newer.

FREE AND OPEN SOURCE
Loft costs nothing. This app, the gateway and the apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows and Linux are open source under the Apache-2.0 licence: github.com/Incremental-AS/loft
The name “Loft by Incremental” and the icon are not part of the licence.

Made by Incremental in Norway. Questions and problems: hello@incremental.no
